epic_title: [Cross-Cutting] Ingest supported datasets and launch analysis views
epic_summary: Provide a consistent client-side path for turning supported files and derived datasets into usable analysis views without requiring intermediate backend preparation.
product_outcome: Analysts can move from supported input files to the correct analysis surface with predictable launch behavior and derived data available across the app.
in_scope: upload supported sequence distance node link tree and date-backed datasets; launch or switch into the intended analysis views; preserve derived datasets for downstream surfaces; handle incomplete or incompatible input gracefully
acceptance_signals: supported datasets launch into the intended analysis surfaces without manual intermediate transforms; downstream views receive the derived client-side data they expect; incompatible or partial input fails predictably instead of producing silent corruption; large reference datasets still produce usable starting state
constraints: Keep ingestion scope client-side and in-browser; do not expand this epic into backend pipelines or mobile upload workflows; treat existing map or analytics integrations as optional dependencies rather than new platform work
notes: Intentional overlap with surface epics. Use this epic when work changes dataset handling across more than one view.

epic_title: [Cross-Cutting] Preserve filtering clustering and visible membership contracts
epic_summary: Keep threshold clustering reveal and downstream membership behavior consistent as analysts move between network-driven views and derived summaries.
product_outcome: Analysts can trust that filtering and reclustering changes update visible membership and dependent summaries coherently across the app.
in_scope: threshold and cluster-size filtering; reveal and membership changes; downstream aggregate map crosstab dashboard and waterfall refresh behavior; table filtering and exact membership contracts; heatmap reactions to shared global settings
acceptance_signals: filtering changes update visible rows nodes links and clusters consistently across affected views; dependent summaries and drilldowns refresh without stale counts; cluster-derived visuals remain coherent after membership changes; empty states appear intentionally when filtering removes all visible data
constraints: Preserve existing client-side filtering semantics instead of inventing a second query model; desktop control density is acceptable; no separate mobile filtering UX is required
notes: Intentional overlap with surface epics. Use this epic for any change that risks inconsistent visible membership between views.

epic_title: [Cross-Cutting] Preserve styling color mapping and rendering controls
epic_summary: Coordinate shared style behavior so labels colors sizes widths and other visual encodings stay interpretable across network and analysis surfaces.
product_outcome: Analysts can change styling and color encodings without losing meaning as they move between views or refresh data.
in_scope: style-file application; field-driven color mapping; label and size controls; node link branch and sequence rendering controls; dashboard-level style propagation; visual encodings that must survive filtering grouping or timeline changes
acceptance_signals: shared style changes propagate to dependent views where expected; field-driven color mappings remain stable through filtering grouping and restoration flows; desktop visual encodings remain legible and interpretable; view-specific styling controls do not break cross-view color contracts
constraints: Do not expand this epic into a new design system or mobile-specific restyling work; stay within existing client-side controls and rendering engines
notes: Intentional overlap with surface epics. Use this epic for changes that affect shared rendering semantics across more than one surface.

epic_title: [Cross-Cutting] Explore time-based states and temporal comparisons
epic_summary: Support the shared timeline and temporal comparison behaviors that let analysts inspect how clustered data changes over time without breaking base view state.
product_outcome: Analysts can step through dated states compare checkpoints and review time-based changes from the same client-side workspace.
in_scope: timeline play and pause controls; manual checkpoints; temporal comparisons in target views; dataset-specific time isolation; chronological ordering for time-based summaries
acceptance_signals: timeline or temporal controls update only the intended surfaces; manual checkpoints and playback preserve stable non-temporal state when they end; temporal comparisons remain chronologically ordered and interpretable; views that are not the timeline target avoid stale or leaked state
constraints: Limit scope to the existing client-side timeline and time-based controls; do not add mobile playback UX or backend scheduling features
notes: Intentional overlap with surface epics. Use this epic for work that changes shared temporal behavior rather than one isolated view only.

epic_summary: Preserve the ability to turn current analysis state into images files tables and shareable artifacts directly from the client-side app.
product_outcome: Analysts can export the visible analysis state into the file types required for review communication and downstream processing.
in_scope: image exports; table and data exports; archive and report outputs; export dialogs and advanced quality controls; surface-specific export fidelity
acceptance_signals: exports reflect the visible state filters ordering or layout that the surface promises to preserve; supported file types remain available from the relevant views; client-side exports succeed without relying on backend report generation; advanced scale and quality controls remain predictable
constraints: Keep export generation client-side; do not expand this epic into server-rendered reporting or mobile sharing flows
notes: Intentional overlap with surface epics. Use this epic when export expectations need to stay coherent across multiple views.

epic_title: [Cross-Cutting] Save restore and reopen state across analysis surfaces
epic_summary: Preserve the saved session and restored-state behaviors that let analysts leave and return to meaningful in-progress work.
product_outcome: Analysts can reopen sessions or views without losing essential rendering layout or comparison state.
in_scope: session save and restore; view reopen persistence; restored map layer and tree state; restored dashboard and derived-view context; stateful layouts that should survive refresh or navigation
acceptance_signals: saved sessions restore the critical controls visuals and layout state promised by each surface; reopen flows do not leak stale selection or orphaned state; restored views remain consistent with current client-side data and filtering; stateful behavior remains deterministic enough for QA review
constraints: Keep persistence client-side and single-user; do not expand this epic into backend storage collaboration features or mobile resume behavior
notes: Intentional overlap with surface epics. Use this epic for persistence or lifecycle work that spans more than one view.

epic_title: [Cross-Cutting] Synchronize shared selection drilldown and workspace composition
epic_summary: Keep cross-view selection drilldown and dashboard composition behavior coherent so analysts can compare surfaces without stale context.
product_outcome: Analysts can inspect related state across views and dashboard panes while keeping selections and drilldowns intentional.
in_scope: shared selection propagation; drilldown clearing rules; dashboard pane composition; cross-view table ordering; interaction patterns that depend on another surface remaining in sync
acceptance_signals: selection propagates only to the surfaces that should react; stale drilldown state is cleared when the upstream selection changes; dashboard layouts keep the right panes connected to shared state; cross-view inspection stays understandable without backend coordination
constraints: Focus on desktop multi-pane workflows and existing client-side shared state; do not expand this epic into role-based collaboration or mobile split-view work
notes: Intentional overlap with surface epics. Use this epic for work that changes how multiple views stay in sync.
